Synopsis:
This chicken is being used as the 'ball' in a goblin sport. The goblins chase it around an enclosure, trying to make it run between two posts so that they can score a 'goal'. It's exhausted and frightened.

Off‑screen a drunken, leering crowd of goblins, wagers and celebratory chaos fill the camp—this is a baited, violent pastime that can escalate (later) to an owlbear chase. In some versions of the scene the player has already been involved nearby—standing on or beside a cage, part of a sabotage that included poisoned beer, or offered a goblin’s suspicious toast—so relations with the goblins are tense and complicated. The chicken has seen other birds killed and is too frightened and worn out to respond when the player urges her to fight back.

- GOB_ChickenChase_Commentator.json: This scene takes place during a goblin camp celebration after the recent hunt: Krolla is a fanatical goblin commentator who runs and taunts participants in the local sport of chicken‑chasing (and, occasionally, larger beasts like an owlbear). She treats the game as sacred, enforces odd house rules (fire is part of play; “only a goblin can win”), and will only let outsiders join if they put up a bet—so player complaints about rules or accusations of a rig are met with scorn and mockery. A strange glowing symbol on the player’s flesh (tied to the illithid tadpole) is noted here and can change how Krolla and the crowd react.

context: You’re watching a ritualized goblin “chicken‑chase” inside a raucous camp: a terrified, exhausted hen is being used like a ball while a drunken, leering crowd of goblins jeer, wager, and celebrate. The bird has been run ragged and has seen other birds killed, so she’s too frightened and worn out to respond when the player urges her to fight back. A fanatical goblin commentator (Krolla) often runs and taunts during the match, enforcing odd house rules and mocking outsiders; nearby goblins (and a bookish sage) may be watching. The player may already have been involved nearby—sabotage, poisoned beer, or a suspicious toast could make relations tense—and a strange glowing mark on the player can change how Krolla and the crowd react; the sport can also later escalate to larger beasts like an owlbear.
